design.title: CyberShield — Real-Time Cyber Threat Intelligence
design.style_name: Dark cyber ops (branded: deep near-black, teal primary, amber accent, mono data type)
design.reference: SOC operations wall / mission-control aesthetic; content-first, minimal decoration

slides.title: Cover
slides.task_brief: COVER. Full-bleed background image: https://z-cdn.chatglm.cn/image-search-mcp/images-ppt/af0c13be7287.jpg (futuristic dark control room with glowing screens) dimmed under a dark overlay (bg gradient from rgba(5,8,13,0.82) to rgba(5,8,13,0.95)) so text passes contrast. Kicker line top-left: 'LIVE THREAT INTELLIGENCE // MISSION WALL'. Main title huge: 'CyberShield' (the word 'Cyber' in --text, 'Shield' in --primary, or a teal underline accent). Subtitle: 'Real-time cyber threat intelligence — aggregated, scored and explained as it happens.' Bottom row: 3 stat chips (mono font, teal value + dim label): '19' LIVE SOURCES · '10' THREAT CATEGORIES · '4 MIN' CACHE REFRESH. Also a small mono tag bottom-right: 'SELF-HOSTED // FREE-HOST READY'.

slides.title: What is CyberShield
slides.task_brief: KEY MESSAGE slide, typographic, no image. Kicker: 'WHAT IT IS'. Big statement (2 lines max): 'One live wall for the world's cybersecurity reporting.' Supporting paragraph (verbatim intent): 'CyberShield is a self-hosted threat-intelligence dashboard. It pulls cybersecurity news from 19 trusted research streams into a single real-time feed — automatically scoring every story for severity, classifying it into threat categories, and explaining what it means on demand with an AI analyst verdict.' Below, 3 compact definition cards: (1) icon 'feed' — 'AGGREGATOR' — '19 streams, one deduplicated wall, refreshed every 4 minutes.'; (2) icon 'psychology' — 'EXPLAINER' — 'AI verdicts in SOC format: threat class, severity, immediate actions.'; (3) icon 'radar' — 'AWARENESS LAYER' — 'Not a scanner or firewall — it keeps you informed, not the network patched.' Small mono footnote: 'RUNS ON A FREE HOSTING TIER — NO PAID SERVICES REQUIRED.'

slides.title: The Problem It Solves
slides.task_brief: SPLIT slide, two columns. Kicker: 'WHY IT EXISTS'. Title: 'Threat intel is scattered. Decisions are slow.' LEFT column card (subtle red/danger tint border, header 'WITHOUT CYBERSHIELD'): 4 bullets — 'Reporting scattered across dozens of blogs, vendor advisories and government feeds'; 'Triage means opening 10+ tabs every morning'; 'Severity is guesswork — a scary headline is not a severity score'; 'Non-specialists freeze at jargon and CVE soup.' RIGHT column card (teal glow, header 'WITH CYBERSHIELD'): 4 matching bullets — 'One wall: 19 streams merged, deduplicated and cached'; 'Machine-speed scoring: every story rated CRITICAL / HIGH / ELEVATED / MODERATE'; '10 threat categories for instant triage'; 'Plain-language AI verdict tells you what happened, why it matters, what to do.' Keep bullets tight; use small mono step numbers 01-04 in each card.

slides.title: How It Works — The Pipeline
slides.layout: 5-step horizontal flow (styled boxes, no SVG connectors)
slides.task_brief: PIPELINE slide. Kicker: 'HOW IT WORKS'. Title: 'From raw feeds to decisions in five stages.' Five numbered stage cards in a horizontal row (use flex; simple CSS arrow glyphs '→' between, no SVG): (01) 'AGGREGATE' — 'Fetches 19 XML streams directly; public-converter relay is the automatic fallback.'; (02) 'DISTILL' — 'Deduplicates stories, picks the best thumbnail, distills an analyst lede.'; (03) 'SCORE' — 'Keyword-and-signal engine rates every story CRITICAL / HIGH / ELEVATED / MODERATE with a 0-100 score.'; (04) 'CLASSIFY' — 'Sorts stories into 10 threat categories from Ransomware to AI Security.'; (05) 'SERVE' — 'Caches the snapshot: 4-minute fresh window, 30-minute stale-safe serve while a background refresh runs.' Bottom strip (mono): 'STACK — NEXT.JS APP ROUTER · PRISMA + SQLITE CACHE · 5 API ENDPOINTS · ZERO DATABASE SERVERS'.

slides.title: Feature — Live Intelligence Feed
slides.task_brief: FEATURE slide. Kicker: 'CORE FEATURE 01'. Title: 'Every stream that matters, on one wall.' Intro line: 'The aggregation engine monitors 19 research streams — direct XML first, with a public-converter relay as automatic fallback so a blocked host never blanks the wall.' Then a 3-column compact grid of all 19 source names, each as a small chip/card with mono short-code: BleepingComputer (BPC), The Hacker News (THN), Threatpost (TPOST), Krebs on Security (KREBS), SecurityWeek (SECWK), Help Net Security (HNS), Infosecurity Magazine (INFOMAG), CyberScoop (SCOOP), The Record (RECORD), Graham Cluley (CLULEY), Malwarebytes Labs (MBLabs), Securelist (SECLST), Unit 42 (U42), Microsoft Security (MSFT), SentinelOne Labs (S1), Schneier on Security (SCHNEIER), Ars Technica Security (ARS), Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), CISA Advisories (CISA). Footer bullets (one line, 3 items): 'Duplicate collapse across outlets' · 'Best-thumbnail extraction per article' · 'Per-story severity + read-time'.

slides.title: Feature — AI Analyst Verdict
slides.task_brief: FEATURE slide, split: left explanation, right a mock verdict panel styled like a terminal report card. Kicker: 'CORE FEATURE 02'. Title: 'An AI analyst reads every story with you.' LEFT: paragraph — 'Open any article and the GLM model distills a SOC-grade verdict in seconds: what happened, why it matters, and the three actions to take first. Verdicts are cached in SQLite keyed by article URL, so a repeat investigation is instant — and REANALYZE re-runs it on demand.' Below, a '3-layer uplink resilience' mini-list (mono numbering): 'L1 Live credentials — direct model call'; 'L2 Forwarded auth — gateway-injected fresh headers'; 'L3 Offline analyst — deterministic heuristic verdict, never dead-ends.' RIGHT: verdict panel card (dark surface, mono type, teal field labels) showing example fields: 'THREAT CLASS: Ransomware Campaign'; 'SEVERITY RATING: CRITICAL 92/100 — active exploitation of unpatched edge devices'; 'WHAT HAPPENED: 2-3 punchy sentences of concrete facts only.'; 'WHY IT MATTERS: defender impact in one or two lines.'; 'IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: ▸ patch exposed services ▸ hunt for IOCs ▸ force credential rotation'. Add tiny dim label under panel: 'CACHED VERDICTS · FORCE REANALYZE · NO INVENTED FACTS'.

slides.title: Feature — CISA KEV Integration
slides.task_brief: FEATURE slide, typographic with a recency scale visual. Kicker: 'CORE FEATURE 03'. Title: 'Known-exploited vulnerabilities, checked mid-investigation.' Paragraph: 'CyberShield serves the official CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog server-side. When a story mentions a CVE, the drawer cross-checks it against the catalog — so you know within seconds whether a flaw is not just published, but actively exploited in the wild.' Reliability row (3 mono chips): '1.7 MB CATALOG — memory-cached' · 'PRIMARY: cisa.gov' · 'FALLBACK: 1:1 auto-synced mirror'. Recency scale — 3 stacked tone cards: 'CRITICAL — added to KEV ≤ 30 days' (red/danger tone), 'HIGH — added ≤ 180 days' (amber tone), 'WATCH — older entries' (dim/teal tone). Footnote: 'Mirror fallback keeps the wall alive if the official edge rejects datacenter traffic.'

slides.title: Feature — Global Situational Awareness
slides.task_brief: FEATURE slide, typographic, no photo. Kicker: 'CORE FEATURE 04'. Title: 'See the world's threat activity, not just a list.' Three large capability tiles in a row: (1) icon 'public' — '3D THREAT GLOBE' — 'A WebGL globe plots global reporting in space — instantly grasp where activity concentrates, powered by three.js with GSAP-driven motion.'; (2) icon 'radar' — 'RADAR BOOT SEQUENCE' — 'Every session starts with a cinematic threat-radar sweep and an honest terminal boot log — the wall is verified live before you read it.'; (3) icon 'graphic_eq' — 'JARVIS VOICE GREETING' — 'An optional voice assistant greeting announces the session; audio unlocks only after a user gesture and is one toggle away from silence.' Bottom mono strip: 'WEBGL GLOBE · GSAP CHOREOGRAPHY · PRIVACY-SAFE AUDIO TOGGLE · REDUCED-MOTION SUPPORTED'.

slides.title: Feature — Investigation & Triage
slides.task_brief: FEATURE slide, split with image right: https://z-cdn.chatglm.cn/image-search-mcp/images-ppt/601e9f74a4a9.jpg (programmer typing code on a laptop at night) in a bordered card with dark gradient overlay. Kicker: 'CORE FEATURE 05'. Title: 'From headline to hands-on in one click.' LEFT text: paragraph — 'Click any story to open the investigation drawer: the full AI verdict, the story's category context, a KEV cross-check for mentioned CVEs, and a clean link out to the original source.' Then '10 category filters' as compact chips (2 rows): All Signals · Ransomware · Zero-Days & CVEs · Data Breaches · APT & Nation-State · Malware · Phishing & Scams · AI Security · Cloud & Enterprise · Mobile & IoT. Below chips, severity strip: CRITICAL (danger) → HIGH (amber) → ELEVATED (teal) → MODERATE (dim) as small labeled swatches. Closing line: 'Triage a full day of global reporting in minutes — filtering beats scrolling.'

slides.title: Who It's For
slides.task_brief: USE-CASE slide, bento grid of 6 tiles (2 rows x 3 cols), each with a Material icon, bold title, one-line use. Kicker: 'WHO IT'S FOR'. Title: 'Built for anyone who needs to know first.' Tiles: (1) icon 'security' — 'SOC & SECURITY TEAMS' — 'A shared live wall for the ops room — everyone reads the same scored feed.'; (2) icon 'manage_accounts' — 'IT MANAGERS' — 'Vendor-neutral awareness: know what is being exploited before it lands in your stack.'; (3) icon 'travel_explore' — 'ANALYSTS & RESEARCHERS' — 'Cross-source dedupe and KEV cross-checks speed up open-source investigations.'; (4) icon 'school' — 'EDUCATORS & STUDENTS' — 'Real cases, real severity scores — the threat landscape as living course material.'; (5) icon 'edit_note' — 'NEWSLETTER & CONTENT CREATORS' — 'Never miss the story: 19 streams, deduplicated, with thumbnails ready to quote.'; (6) icon 'insights' — 'EXECUTIVES' — 'The five-minute morning read: highest-severity items first, plain-language verdicts.'

slides.title: Use-Case Scenarios
slides.task_brief: USE-CASE slide, 2x2 grid of scenario cards, each with mono step arrows showing input → output. Kicker: 'HOW TEAMS USE IT'. Title: 'Four scenarios, four wins.' Cards: (1) 'MORNING BRIEFING' — 'Open the wall → scan scored headlines → read only CRITICAL/HIGH verdicts. Result: situational awareness before the first coffee.'; (2) 'INCIDENT TRIAGE' — 'Paste a live article → AI verdict returns class, severity, 3 immediate actions. Result: defensible next steps in under a minute.'; (3) 'VULNERABILITY WATCH' — 'A CVE appears in a story → KEV cross-check shows exploit status + recency tone. Result: patch priorities that reflect reality.'; (4) 'TEAM AWARENESS' — 'Put the wall on the ops-room display → globe, ticker and severity tones keep everyone oriented. Result: one shared picture of the threat landscape.' Keep each card to the same 3-line rhythm: WHAT YOU DO → WHAT YOU GET (Result line highlighted in teal).

slides.title: Deploy Anywhere
slides.task_brief: PRACTICALITY slide. Kicker: 'RUN IT YOUR WAY'. Title: 'Free-tier friendly by design, not by accident.' LEFT: 3 big stat blocks (mono numerals): '60s' — 'function ceilings baked into every route — survives Vercel Hobby limits'; '0' — 'paid dependencies — public RSS, converter relay and mirror fallbacks only'; '1' — 'file SQLite database — copy the folder, move the deployment'. RIGHT: bullet card 'Deployment paths' with 4 items: 'VERCEL — push, import, deploy; time limits pre-configured in the route files'; 'DOCKER — single Dockerfile, .dockerignore included'; 'SELF-HOST — any Node/Bun runtime; portable .env with a relative database path'; 'DATA OWNERSHIP — self-host and your reading history stays yours.' Footer mono strip: 'NO VERCEL.JSON NEEDED — DURATIONS LIVE IN THE ROUTES · POSTINSTALL RUNS PRISMA GENERATE'.

slides.title: Closing
slides.task_brief: CLOSING slide, typographic, centered. Kicker: 'CYBERSHIELD'. Huge closing line: 'Stay ahead of the threat.' Sub-line: 'Aggregated intelligence, machine-speed scoring, plain-language verdicts — on a wall you own.' Recap strip of 6 small mono chips in one row: '19 SOURCES' · 'AI VERDICTS' · 'KEV CROSS-CHECK' · '3D THREAT GLOBE' · 'VOICE GREETING' · 'FREE-HOST READY'. Bottom CTA line: 'Download the package → deploy to your platform → informed in under five minutes.' Tiny dim footer: 'CYBERSHIELD // REAL-TIME CYBER THREAT INTELLIGENCE'.
